summary_html: A **court reverses or vacates** a CPS or agency decision due to procedural error, insufficient evidence, or constitutional violation. Federal review data (CFSR, ASFA) tracks judicial determinations on reasonable efforts and due process.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — judicial findings of 'reasonable efforts' compliance  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of judicial/agency conformity  
- **42 U.S.C. § 1983** — civil-rights remedy for unconstitutional removals (14th & 4th Amendments).

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Lee TT. v. Dowling
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals held that the 'some credible evidence' standard for retaining an indicated report in the Statewide Central Register violates federal due process to the extent the report is disseminated to provider and licensing agencies, and that a subject is entitled to a pre-deprivation hearing at which the agency must prove the abuse or maltreatment by a fair preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The Court annulled agency determinations made under an unconstitutional standard, the model for judicial reversal of a substantiation.
key_cases.quote: subjects are entitled to a predeprivation hearing to determine by a fair preponderance of the evidence whether reports of abuse can be substantiated and relevant to future employment or licensure

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Elizabeth B. v. New York State Office of Children & Family Services
key_cases.court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, Third Department
key_cases.holding: The Third Department annulled the portion of the OCFS determination that maintained an indicated report of inadequate guardianship against a mother who was herself the victim of domestic violence, ordering the report unfounded, expunged and sealed, because the minimum-degree-of-care inquiry must account for the risks and constraints she actually faced.
key_cases.relevance: This is a current example of an article 78 court annulling an agency substantiation on the merits.
key_cases.quote: Respondent misconstrues this standard as one that cannot be "modified or excused because a parent is under stress or fear."

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed a termination order, holding for the first time that the right to assigned counsel in proceedings to terminate parental rights necessarily includes the right to effective assistance, and that counsel who had never spoken with the parent before the fact-finding hearing and announced he would remain silent did not provide it.
key_cases.relevance: This is the current New York authority for vacating an agency-sought order because of a procedural failure in the parent's representation.
key_cases.quote: the right to assigned counsel in proceedings to terminate parental rights necessarily encompasses the right to effective assistance of counsel

key_cases.holding: The Court held that an agency seeking termination for permanent neglect must affirmatively plead in detail and prove by clear and convincing evidence that it exercised diligent efforts to strengthen the parent-child relationship, and that failure to carry that threshold burden requires dismissal of the petition as to that parent.
key_cases.relevance: The Court reinstated Family Court's dismissal, reversing an appellate ruling that had excused the agency's failures.
key_cases.quote: It has declared as a matter of public policy that the State may not intervene to terminate a parent's rights when assistance in strengthening the family has not been forthcoming

key_cases.court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, Second Department
key_cases.holding: Reaching the merits under the mootness exception and reversing, the Second Department held that a parent excluded from the home by a full stay-away order of protection in an article 10 proceeding is entitled to a prompt Family Court Act § 1028 hearing applying the imminent-risk standard, because such an order is functionally equivalent to removal of the children from his care.
key_cases.relevance: The court reversed Family Court's denial of a § 1028 hearing and rejected contrary trial-level decisions.
key_cases.quote: it must be governed by the same legal standards as are provided for removal of a child in Family Court Act §§ 1027 and 1028
